findings.title: The 'held out' set is byte-identical to the training set; every reported accuracy is a TRAINING accuracy
findings.evidence: Line 40: `NTR, NTE, STEPS, LR = 1500, 1500, 700, 0.05`. Lines 160-163: `rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd)` / `Etr, ytr = worldfn(rng, NTR)` / `Ete, yte = worldfn(np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd), NTE)  # same world, fresh draw` / `Ete, yte = Ete[:NTE], yte[:NTE]`. Both calls use the same seed 1000+sd and the same n=1500, so the generator draws the same A, B, C and the same E. Line 163 slices 1500 to 1500 (no-op). Verified by exec-ing the definitions portion outside the repo: for all four world functions and all 5 seeds, `E identical=True  y identical=True  n_tr=1500 n_te=1500`. Line 173 prints `{NTR} train / {NTE} held out`, i.e. '1500 train / 1500 held out', which is false. Line 147-148: `out, _ = forward(p, Ete, order)` / `return float((np.argmax(out, axis=1) == yte).mean())` -- evaluated on the training data.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The numbers 0.9689 / 0.9471 / 0.9312 / 0.9448 / 0.7245 / 0.7307 and the bag gaps 0.13-0.15 are all train-set fit, not generalisation. The commit message and the script's banner both present them as held-out. With 480 trainable parameters on 1500 items and 700 full-batch Adam steps, arm ranking on unseen data is unknown; mismatched-order chains (fitting a non-realizable function) could over-fit more than the matching chain, so the true held-out order gap could be larger OR smaller. The conclusion cannot be read as stated until re-run with a distinct test draw (different seed or n for the test call).

findings.title: POSITIVE control is a capacity/interaction test, not an order-matching test: chain arms have 480 trainable parameters with recurrent cross-type interaction, the bag has 224 and is purely additive
findings.evidence: Lines 91-95 `init`: W = K*(DE*H) = 4*40 = 160; U = K*(H*H) = 4*64 = 256 (`np.zeros((H, H)) if bag else rng.normal(...)`); b = K*H = 32; R = H*NCLS = 32. Chain total 480; bag trainable 224 (U frozen: line 129 `g["U"][j] = np.zeros((H, H))`, verified U stays exactly zero under the Adam update at lines 141-143). Line 101 bag forward: `h = sum(np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p["W"][j] + p["b"][j]) for j in range(K))` -- a sum over types, no term couples two types. Line 105 chain forward: `h = np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p["W"][j] + h @ p["U"][j].T + p["b"][j])` -- multiplicative interaction via U. The world (line 60) `s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T)` has the chain's exact functional form, so the matching chain is realizable and the bag is not. Line 204: `pos_ok = (A[cas][0] > A[bag][0] + 0.02) and (Cc[rev][0] > Cc[bag][0] + 0.02)` compares matching CHAIN vs BAG only. Commit: 'BAG mechanism-free loses by 0.13-0.15 everywhere ordered' while the MISMATCHED chains sit within 0.0219 / 0.0136 of the matching chain, i.e. a wrong-order chain still beats the bag by roughly 0.11-0.13.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: 'Order matters' in the commit is almost entirely 'a recurrent chain beats an additive bag' -- an asymmetry in parameter count (480 vs 224) and representational class, present with any order. The order-specific effect is only the +0.0219 / -0.0136 match-vs-mismatch gap. The positive control therefore does not certify that the harness can detect order-matching at the 0.02 scale it then uses as the verdict threshold.

findings.title: Conditions (a) and (c) are mirror images measuring the same quantity twice; the 0.02 threshold falls between the two realisations, so 'HELD' vs 'FAILED' is a threshold artifact
findings.evidence: Lines 181-182: `make_world(r, CAS_ORDER, n)` and `make_world(r, REVERSED, n)` with the same seeds 1000+sd (line 160). make_world (lines 51-54) draws A, B, C, E from the rng before the order is used, so (a) and (c) share identical A, B, C, E; only the composition order at line 60 differs (verified: `E identical=True`, label agreement 0.2113-0.3300 per seed). E's K type channels are i.i.d. (line 54 `E = rng.normal(0, 1, (n, K, DE))`), so relabelling types maps world-CAS/arm-CAS onto world-REV/arm-REV exactly in distribution. Both non-matching arms are full derangements in both worlds: verified `positions matched = 0/4` for REV and RANDFIX vs world CAS and for CAS and RANDFIX vs world REV. Lines 224-225: `d_a = A[cas][0] - max(A[rev][0], A[ran][0])` (>= +0.0219) and `d_c = Cc[cas][0] - Cc[rev][0]` (-0.0136). Line 232 thresholds `d_a > 0.02` and `d_c < -0.02`.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Match-minus-mismatch was realised as >= 0.0219 in (a) and 0.0136 in (c); the registered 0.02 line sits between two draws of the same effect. That the sign pattern flips with the world's order actually supports 'the world sets the winner', but the HELD/FAILED labels the program printed reflect noise around a fixed constant, not a difference between the CAS order and the reversed order. The registered prediction (c) 'FAILED' is not evidence that CAS resists losing.

findings.title: 5 seeds, absolute thresholds not calibrated to noise, per-arm sd instead of paired-difference sd; +0.0219 vs threshold 0.02 is a 0.0019 margin that the commit itself labels '~1 seed sd'
findings.evidence: Line 41 `SEEDS = 5`. Line 167: `return {k: (float(np.mean(v)), float(np.std(v, ddof=1))) for k, v in acc.items()}` -- the sd is across the 5 seed-level accuracies (seed sd, not item sd), and the per-seed vectors are discarded here. Lines 159-166: every arm shares the same world (Etr/ytr) per seed and the same init seed `np.random.default_rng(7000 + sd)` (verified: the three chain arms have identical initial W, U, b, R), so the design is PAIRED, but lines 224-226 compare unpaired means of means and line 230 prints `seed sd approx {max(Bb[k][1] for k in (cas, rev, ran)):.4f}` = the largest single-arm sd in (b), not the sd of the CAS-minus-other difference. Thresholds are fixed constants: line 204 `+ 0.02`, line 206 `< 0.05`, line 232 `> 0.02`, `< 0.03`, `< -0.02`. Commit: '(a) ... +0.0219 (~1 seed sd)' and '(b) ... seed sd 0.0301'. With per-arm seed sd 0.0301, SE of a 5-seed mean is 0.0301/sqrt(5) = 0.0135 and an unpaired difference SE is about 0.019 -- the same size as the 0.02 threshold. The paired-difference sd, which could be smaller, is never computed or printed; the (a) and (c) sds exist only in un-captured stdout.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Neither +0.0219 (a) nor -0.0136 (c) nor -0.0061 (b) can be distinguished from seed noise from what is reported. The HELD/FAILED labels are readings of a fixed constant against a noisy mean with n=5 and no test statistic. The only differences clearly above noise are chain-vs-bag (0.13-0.15), which is the capacity asymmetry, not order.

findings.title: Prediction (b) 'all fixed orders tie' holds by symmetry of the world, so it cannot inform about CAS
findings.evidence: Lines 72-77: `order = rng.permutation(K)` redrawn per item, then `s = np.tanh(E[i, order[j], :] @ A[j] + B[j] @ s)`. Because the true order is a uniform random permutation per item and E's type channels are i.i.d., any fixed arm order is equally mismatched in distribution; the three fixed-order arms are exchangeable. Line 23: `The prediction is FALSIFIED if the CAS arm wins in (b)` -- a clause that can only trip by noise. Line 226 `d_b = Bb[cas][0] - max(Bb[rev][0], Bb[ran][0])` additionally biases d_b negative (max of two noisy arms).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The 'DEAD TIE' in (b) is guaranteed by construction and carries no information about the CAS order; it functions only as a noise-level readout (0.0301). It should not be counted as a held falsifiable prediction.

p6_lenses.world_generation_answer_key: The label is a deterministic function of the evidence E with no noise. Lines 48-62 `make_world`: per condition, A (K matrices DE x H), B (K matrices H x H), C (H x NCLS) and E (n x K x DE, i.i.d. normal type channels) are drawn from the seed BEFORE the order is used; then line 60 `s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T)` composes types in `true_order` and line 61 `y = np.argmax(s @ C, axis=1)`. The chain arm's forward (line 105) has exactly this functional form (W<->A, U<->B, R<->C, b=0), so the arm whose order equals the world's order is the generator itself (realizable); any other fixed order is a mismatch of equal capacity; the bag (line 101) cannot represent the cross-type interaction at all. The true order is swept as a condition (lines 180-185): (a) CAS (0,1,2,3), (c) REVERSED (3,2,1,0), (b) per-item random permutation (lines 72-77, no fixed order can match), NEG no-structure bag world (line 86). Consequences verified outside the repo: (a) and (c) share identical A, B, C, E for each seed (only composition order differs; label agreement 0.2113-0.3300); REVERSED and RANDOM_FIXED (2,0,3,1) both match 0/4 positions of both world orders, so both 'other' arms are full derangements; (b) makes all fixed orders exchangeable, so its tie is by construction. The world's true order is therefore the answer key: the arm that carries it wins by realizability, whichever order it is -- which is exactly what the script set out to show, but the design makes (a) and (c) two draws of one quantity rather than two independent tests.

p6_lenses.arms_matched: Parameters (lines 91-95, K=4, DE=5, H=8, NCLS=4): chain arms (P5 CAS, P6a reversed, P6b random fixed) W 4x(5x8)=160, U 4x(8x8)=256, b 4x8=32, R 8x4=32 = 480 trainable. BAG arm: W 160, b 32, R 32 = 224 trainable; U is 256 zeros (line 93), receives zero gradient (line 129) and verified to stay exactly zero under the Adam update (lines 141-143) -- so the bag has 224 trainable vs 480, and no cross-type interaction term at all (line 101 additive sum vs line 105 recurrent `h @ p[\"U\"][j].T`). Compute per step: chain forward ~ K*n*DE*H + K*n*H*H + n*H*NCLS = 240000 + 384000 + 48000 = 672000 multiply-adds; bag forward 288000 plus a recomputed tanh in its backward (line 125) -- chain is roughly 2.3x the bag's compute per step. Steps: 700 for every arm (line 40, line 116). Optimiser: full-batch Adam, beta1 .9, beta2 .999, eps 1e-8, bias-corrected (lines 141-146), LR 0.05 for every arm (line 143, 146). Init: all three chain arms identical at init (seed 7000+sd, verified); bag shares the chain's W and b but its R is a different draw (line 93 skips the U draws). Worlds paired across arms per seed (lines 159-166). Asymmetry that explains 'order matters' without order: the chain-vs-bag gap (0.13-0.15) is a capacity/representation gap -- 480 vs 224 parameters and recurrent interaction vs additive -- and mismatched-order chains also beat the bag by roughly 0.11-0.13; the order-specific gap is only +0.0219 / -0.0136. Hyperparameters were not tuned per arm (single setting), so chain-vs-chain comparisons are fair; the positive control (line 204) is not.
p6_lenses.verdict_on_specific_cas_order_value: NOT ESTABLISHED IN EITHER DIRECTION BY THIS SCRIPT AS COMMITTED. What survives: the sign pattern (the CAS-ordered arm is best when the world is CAS-ordered, 0.9689 vs 0.9471, and worst-of-the-pair when the world is reversed, 0.9312 vs 0.9448) is consistent with 'the arm carrying the world's own order wins by realizability, whichever order that is', and (a)/(c) are mirror images of one another by construction, so nothing here favours P>C>E>O specifically. What does not survive: (1) every number is a training-set accuracy (lines 160-163), so no generalisation claim exists; (2) the status word CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED was not emitted by the program -- with (c) FAILED the script printed the line-251-253 'PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED / do NOT substitute a new hypothesis' branch, and the commit message substituted one anyway; (3) the order-specific effects +0.0219, -0.0136, -0.0061 are at the 5-seed noise level (seed sd 0.0301; author's own '~1 seed sd'), tested against fixed constants 0.02/0.03/0.05 with no paired analysis, and the same match-vs-mismatch quantity realised as >=0.0219 in (a) and 0.0136 in (c) straddles the 0.02 line; (4) 'order matters' is carried by the chain-vs-bag gap, which is a 480-vs-224-parameter, recurrent-vs-additive capacity asymmetry, not an order effect; (5) 3 of 24 orders tested. Plain reading: the specific CAS order P>C>E>O shows no intrinsic advantage in this harness, but the harness as committed cannot license that as a measured result either -- it is a training-fit readout with a prose-assigned status.
